title: IMAP efficiency review: no actionable issues
description:
Efficiency review of the four IMAP4rev2 files (stoa-db727e07 wave):
  crates/imap/src/session/mod.rs
  crates/imap/src/session/commands.rs
  crates/imap/src/session/mailbox.rs
  crates/imap/tests/e2e_smoke.rs

Findings per checklist item:

1. format!("{cap}") in ENABLE handler (mod.rs:474)
   CapabilityEnable in imap-types 2.0.0-alpha.6 has no typed variant for
   IMAP4rev2; it parses as Other(CapabilityEnableOther(atom)). The inner
   Atom is not accessible without coupling to library internals. format!()
   is the only clean approach. ENABLE is a once-per-session cold path
   (one-way latch, called at most once after auth). No change warranted.

2. capability_list() allocates a new Vec per CAPABILITY command
   Builds 8-9 enum values per call. CAPABILITY is sent 2-3 times per
   session at most. Allocation cost is negligible. Caching would add
   complexity with no measurable benefit. No change warranted.

3. handle_namespace() allocates on every call
   Builds one Vec<Namespace> per NAMESPACE command. NAMESPACE is issued
   at most once per session. Allocation is one heap element. No change
   warranted.

4. max_command_size cast correctness
   .min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32 is correct; the guard prevents truncation.
   Adjacent saturating_add(1) (u32 + 1) handles u32::MAX edge case
   correctly. Config default is 8 KiB so this is academic. No change
   warranted.

5. TLS cert generated per test in e2e_smoke.rs
   make_test_tls_pair() generates a fresh cert per TLS test. Three TLS
   tests exist. Sharing via OnceLock would risk inter-test coupling and
   flakiness under parallel test execution. Per-test isolation is correct.
   No change warranted.

Decision: no efficiency issues worth addressing. IMAP sessions are not
hot paths; allocations are bounded to once-per-session or once-per-command
frequencies.
